welcome.title: Welcome to DQM Onboarding
welcome.intro: The National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) uses <nhsnlink>NHSNLink</nhsnlink>, an open-source Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (<fhir>FHIR®</fhir>) application, to enable reporting of digital quality measures (dQMs) to NHSN. The enrollment information populated in this web form supports secure and successful authentication of NHSNLink with your facility’s FHIR endpoint, adequate understanding by NHSN of your FHIR data submissions, and successful reporting of dQMs to NHSN.
welcome.audienceBody: The onboarding steps that follow should be completed by the site’s information technology team.
welcome.workflowBody: Each onboarding section includes downloadable materials and instructions to facilitate completion. Onboarding steps do not have to be completed at one time; the user can save the information and return at a later time.

fhirServerInfo.title: FHIR Server Information
fhirServerInfo.subtitleSuffix: standard to connect with your facility's EHR system. Please provide the technical information needed to securely connect your EHR FHIR APIs to NHSNLink.

fields.baseUrlTooltip: The FHIR base URL used to access your facility's FHIR resources. Example: https://ehr.example.org/fhir/r4
fields.jwksInstructions: {{vendor}} facilities now support JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) based authentication. This is enabled directly by your facility's EHR administrator from the {{vendor}} vendor portal — no credentials need to be entered here. Download the instructions below and provide them to your EHR administrator to enable JWKS for NHSNLink.
fields.maxConcurrentRequestsTooltip: NHSNLink is capable of querying resources concurrently for reported patients. This setting throttles how many requests will run concurrently against the facility FHIR server.
fields.maxRetriesTooltip: If NHSNLink experiences an issue while querying the facility FHIR server, it can retry the request. This setting determines the maximum number of retries NHSNLink can attempt for a given FHIR resource request. The value must be between 0 and 10.
fields.minPullTimeTooltip: Specifies the earliest time NHSNLink is allowed to start querying the facility FHIR server for patient resources.
fields.maxPullTimeTooltip: Specifies the time NHSNLink stops querying the facility FHIR server for patient resources.
fields.lagTooltip: A lag time can be applied for each patient being reported to ensure that data related to the visit has settled prior to acquiring it from the facility FHIR server, for example so lab results can be finalized and medication orders completed. Scheduled reports wait until each patient in the census is accounted for, even if the applied lag extends beyond the reporting period.

census.title: Patients of Interest Configuration
census.intro1: Patients of Interest (POI) are the patients included for NHSN ACH dQM surveillance and measure evaluation. POI includes patients receiving care in inpatient, emergency department, observation, and short-stay settings during the surveillance measurement period.
census.intro2: NHSNLink must identify the POI before retrieving the FHIR resources needed for measure evaluation. How the POI is identified depends on your EHR and configuration. The following steps will guide you through configuring how NHSNLink identifies your facility's POI.

epic.subtitle: For Epic facilities using automated POI acquisition, NHSNLink uses configured Epic system patient lists to identify currently admitted and recently discharged patients. The Epic List API has a limit of 1500 patients returned with any one query, so building six separate system lists is recommended to keep daily queries well under the 1500 limit threshold and to avoid missing patients with short admissions.

locationOrg.title: Organization Identification
locationOrg.intro: If your health system uses multiple FHIR endpoints, NHSNLink needs to determine which facility in the health system each patient encounter belongs to. Use the form below to help identify your specific facility in the FHIR data. No additional configuration is needed if your facility's FHIR data is not shared with other facilities in your health system.

managingOrg.tooltip: Add the identifiers of the FHIR Organization resources that manage your facility's Locations. NHSNLink uses these to determine which Locations belong to your facility.

locationType.intro: Cerner Millennium supports querying Locations by physical type. NHSNLink can use this capability to search for Locations tagged as "Site" which typically can be used to correlate Location resources that represent your reporting facility organization. The search button below can assist in applying these mappings.
locationType.tooltip: Add the Location.type code and alias values that identify your facility's Locations. Use Search Cerner Site Locations to find and add these automatically.

locationIdentifier.instructions: Instructions are available to download here with more information on how to identify the FHIR Location resource that represents your reporting facility.
locationIdentifier.listLabel: Location Identifier System / Location Identifier Code
locationIdentifier.tooltip: Add the identifier system and code that uniquely identify your facility's Location resource in the FHIR data.

customFhirPath.label: Custom FHIR Path
customFhirPath.tooltip: Enter a FHIRPath expression NHSNLink can evaluate against a Location resource to determine whether it belongs to your reporting facility.

encounter.title: Encounter Mapping
encounter.subtitle: The NHSN measures evaluated by Link conform to the FHIR <uscore>US Core</uscore> implementation guide. This guide is a set of rules and best practices that help healthcare providers share patient information accross the United States. In this rule set, all patient FHIR <encounters>Encounters</encounters> must have an Encounter Type (e.g. e-mail consultation, surgical day-care, skilled nursing, rehabilitation) that maps to Patient Encounter Procedure SNOMED or CPT codes. More information on those requirements can be found <valueset>here</valueset>. Below is a form to associate your local Encounter.type codes to their corresponding SMOMED or CPT codes.

fields.codeSystemsHint: Add each source code system your facility's local Encounter.type codes come from. Within each code system, map its local codes to the corresponding CPT or SNOMED reference code.
